description: Team of 4 doing a hackathon for the first time
summary: Our challenge was to make a mars data gathering mission for young children, our project enables kids to research and collect data through a series of experiments which include, Soil collection, Plant growth, mini-game quizzes and more! All tailored to intrigue young minds and let them learn at their own pace. Our game is made with human drawn graphics fit to excite kids!
details:
Together our team cultivated a perfect balance to ensure a fully functional Martian data collection mission for a team of 4 astronauts! This single player game ensures that players will surely have a taste or astronaut life alongside fun experiments on mars! Our team's creativity is evidently visible through hand made graphics for starters, our project's colour scheme, formats, fonts were all picked and implemented by our team to give our app a theme that is sure to excite! Our team considered factors such as how in depth the information added must be. Its focus into curating the game for children of specified age enabled us to ensure the game's limits of information and which areas we'll need to work on specifically. We used Godot for making the entire project, aided with Ibispaint for graphics alongside GitHub as our repository ensuring coordinated transfer of all resources.

Our project includes human coded works from the drawings to the game itself, all of it is made by human. Our research was also cultivated entirely by humans. We began with main game elements then worked inwards starting from our selection of experiments to the characters. Distributing work evenly. Sanah, our head graphic design and research assistant supplied the team with all the graphics you see scattered across the game. These eye catching elements capture the interest of our target audience, children 7-12, perfectly. Then there’s the work of our programmers, Aaryesh, Ahlam and Liam, with Liam working on character movement as Aaryesh works out the experiments and game elements, with Ahlam’s assistance with the same. Aaryesh and Ahlam, team leaders of the group ensured work remained smooth throughout, taking turns to take checks on work management and assist with errors. They also worked on research for the same.
